tasks.short: Find unavailable merchandise and arrange a store transfer or special order.

steps.what: Clarify the customer's item, acceptable alternatives, budget and delivery needs.
Search the {OPS_SYSTEM} for stock at other locations.
Call another store or supplier to confirm availability and delivery.
Explain price and timing, then obtain the customer's choice.
Enter and submit the agreed order in the {OPS_SYSTEM} or {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Send the customer an order confirmation and later delivery updates through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure cross-store stock search in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, then connect available supplier confirmations from the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. A structured order form checks item, price and delivery before the sales associate approves submission; the {WORKFLOW} sends factual status updates through {EMAIL}. Calls remain for unavailable feeds and uncertain commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock visibility, supplier confirmation and order entry often sit in separate systems. Local software can already solve parts of this.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock interfaces and configurable notifications cover routine cases. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining connectors.
tasks.still_hard: Displayed stock may be unavailable, reserved or damaged. Suppliers without reliable interfaces still require calls.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the customer will compromise on and explain uncertain delivery promises.

ambition.what: Reconsider a delayed special order when a faster store transfer becomes available.

tasks.altitude: More time goes to customer choices and delivery exceptions. Purchasing, reservation and discount authority stay within existing limits.

reach.task: Resolve delayed orders and failed store transfers.
reach.learn: Reservation expiry, fulfilment statuses and transfer cancellation rules.

evidence.claim: Availability and item-history records are established software capabilities, although the cited example concerns rentals.
Cross-store lookup, structured ordering and status notifications can use deterministic integrations; this exact design is an extrapolation.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The baseline includes cross-store stock screens, phone confirmation and manual order submission.
Calls remain substantial, but reliable stock feeds can replace some routine confirmation.
Order submission requires the customer's agreement and the associate's final check.
Access estimates include customer-data permissions and any consultation required by national rules.
Customer details follow GDPR access, purpose and retention limits.
unknowns: Which stock, reservation and supplier interfaces are available?
How often does displayed stock fail physical confirmation?
Who may commit spending or reserve stock, and within which limits?
Which customer update channels and data uses are authorised?
research_questions: Can stock be reserved atomically rather than merely displayed?
Do supplier interfaces support duplicate-safe submission and cancellation?
new_work: Handle stale stock, failed reservations and uncertain delivery dates.
Maintain supplier mappings, connector credentials and notification templates.

tasks.short: Clean merchandise shelves, counters and tables.

steps.what: Inspect surfaces and identify spills, fragile goods and areas needing cleaning.
Move merchandise as needed, wipe surfaces and return goods safely.
Check that surfaces are clean, dry and ready for customer use.

tasks.design: Keep inspection, wiping and the final condition check with store staff. Improve access to suitable supplies and practical cleaning instructions; no software build is justified for this task alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires physical access and manipulation around changing merchandise layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: No relevant software breakthrough changes the physical task. Better supplies and layout may help independently of AI.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile displays, sticky spills and customer traffic require hands-on work.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hazards and clean around merchandise without damaging it or obstructing customers.
tasks.altitude: The person's week and decision rights do not change through software automation of this task.

reach.task: Plan cleaning coverage around busy trading periods.
reach.learn: Traffic patterns, cleaning times and safe access to displays.

evidence.claim: Cleaning occupied retail surfaces remains physical work; a workflow application does not perform it.

assumptions: Time shares are estimates for ordinary shelves, counters and tables.
Physical cleaning dominates time; the prior's decision-heavy split is not used.
No new monitoring, records or application is introduced.
Run cost refers to the proposed technology change, not existing cleaning labour or supplies.
unknowns: Which surfaces, merchandise and cleaning materials are involved?
Is cleaning shared with a facilities team?
Are existing instructions adequate for the surfaces concerned?
research_questions: Would relocating supplies or changing display access reduce cleaning time?

tasks.short: Keep sales records complete, accurate and available for reconciliation.

steps.what: Retrieve daily sales records from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Match paper receipts, vouchers and special-order evidence to recorded sales.
Copy sales figures into the local {SPREADSHEET} sales register.
Compare totals and identify missing or duplicate entries in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Investigate exceptions and confirm authorised corrections in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Archive sales evidence in {DOCS} and send the finance team a summary through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Feed sales events from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system into the {ERP}, using transaction identifiers to prevent duplicates. Deterministic checks link digital evidence in {DOCS} and produce an exception queue, replacing the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register. Staff investigate unresolved evidence and confirm corrections before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local registers bridge gaps between sales, evidence storage and finance. Different identifiers and paper exceptions make those bridges costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, interfaces and configurable archives cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can make transaction mapping and reconciliation checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Paper evidence, offline sales, returns and inconsistent identifiers still need investigation. A matching total alone does not prove completeness.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why a transaction differs and distinguish a genuine correction from an unsupported adjustment.

ambition.what: A receipt-to-sale evidence pack for the finance team.

tasks.altitude: The associate works through evidence exceptions instead of copying sales totals. Correction rights remain within existing limits.

reach.task: Trace special-order deposits, cancellations and fulfilment against sales records.
reach.learn: Transaction identifiers, deposit treatment and order-to-sale status mapping.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed X-Series exposes register closing information and expected payment totals.
Duplicate-safe sales ingestion, evidence linking and completeness checks are deterministic integration patterns; the full proposed design is not a documented case.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The baseline has a digital sales source, a local spreadsheet bridge and some paper evidence.
The prior's large in-person share is not imposed on a predominantly records task.
Evidence with stable digital identifiers is matched automatically; paper exceptions remain manual.
Associates may confirm routine corrections within existing permissions; other adjustments are escalated.
Access and consultation estimates cover employee-linked records under GDPR and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Does a duplicate local register exist, and what purpose does it serve?
Which sales, return and deposit events are available through exports or interfaces?
Which records need statutory retention, and for how long?
Would the proposed reporting change the use of employee data?
research_questions: Can source transaction identifiers survive exports, returns and finance posting?
How will reconciliation detect missing events rather than only mismatched totals?
new_work: Review unmatched evidence and failed imports.
Maintain transaction mappings, access permissions and retention settings.
Check reconciliation coverage after sales or finance system changes.
Escalate corrections beyond the associate's authority.

tasks.short: Open and close registers, reconcile takings and prepare cash deposits.

steps.what: Count the opening float and check physical cash custody.
Enter the opening count and open the {OTHER} point-of-sale register.
At closing, count cash and separate charge slips, coupons and vouchers.
Retrieve expected payment totals from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Compare counted amounts with expected totals on the paper cash-up sheet.
Recount discrepancies and investigate missing payment evidence.
Review the reconciliation and approve closing adjustments and the deposit amount.
Retain the next float and seal the approved cash deposit.
Hand over the sealed deposit and retain the deposit receipt.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale system to collect counts, calculate payment variances and retain closing evidence. Use its existing approval flow, or configure the {WORKFLOW}, to approve adjustments and deposit amounts before passing closing records to the {ERP}. Cash counting, sealing and custody remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected totals may already be automated, while paper cash-up and finance handoffs persist. Physical cash handling cannot be removed by a connector.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing closing functions already calculate expected totals and accept staff counts. Configuration and a small finance connector can remove duplicate calculations and filing.
tasks.still_hard: Someone must count and secure cash, investigate discrepancies and preserve custody. Incorrect counts can make a balanced report misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unexplained variance and take responsibility for cash custody and authorised adjustments.
tasks.altitude: Less closing time goes to calculations and copying figures. Cash custody and adjustment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Review unresolved closing variances and plan cash-control improvements.
reach.learn: Payment settlement timing, custody evidence and causes of reconciliation differences.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed X-Series closing functions show expected totals by payment type and accept staff-entered counts.
In the Netherlands, employee-data and monitoring arrangements can require works-council consent.
Physical counting and cash custody remain manual in the proposed configuration.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The baseline uses a digital till and paper cash-up sheet, not a spreadsheet.
One person may hold several listed roles; the steps still mark custody and approval changes.
Existing closing functions can replace manual variance calculations.
Deposit handover follows the supervisor's approved instruction; it needs no second software approval.
Access estimates include consultation where employee-linked reporting changes under national rules.
GDPR access and retention controls apply to employee-linked closing records.
Existing cash equipment is retained; no robotics or new surveillance is assumed.
unknowns: Which closing and approval functions are already enabled?
Who counts, approves, seals and deposits cash?
Which evidence is still required on paper?
Are cash-up reports employee-linked, and would their use change?
Does the finance interface support approved closing records and later corrections?
research_questions: Can the existing register enforce a blind count before showing expected cash?
How are late settlements, refunds and deposit receipts linked to the correct closing?
new_work: Review unresolved variances and approve adjustments.
Monitor failed closing transfers to finance.
Maintain payment mappings, approval limits and access permissions.
Check that closing evidence and physical deposit receipts remain traceable.

role.altitude: The largest gains come from connected stock information and removing duplicate sales administration. Customer conversations, cleaning and cash custody remain substantial parts of the week; new commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Order clerk: trace special orders, deposits and delivery exceptions.
Retail supervisor: interpret closing exceptions and improve cash-control routines.
skills_to_grow: Read stock availability and reservation states.
Trace sales, deposits and returns through shared identifiers.
Investigate reconciliation exceptions using source evidence.
Explain uncertain fulfilment options to customers.
role.ambitious_version: Become a store fulfilment specialist who resolves difficult availability requests and follows delayed orders through to delivery, within agreed reservation and spending limits.
